claims.notes: A DOCUMENTED CHICAGO HOUSE WITH A CORNER AND A FOOTPRINT: 16 by 30 feet, at Lasalle and Lake. This is the single most directly buildable line in the month. It gives a named intersection, a plan dimension in feet, and a date — offered 22 April, still standing and untenanted on 21 May 1834, possession on the first of June. Four hundred and eighty square feet is a small two-room or three-room dwelling, and the 30-foot dimension is almost certainly the frontage-or-depth of a single-pile plan; WHICH of the two runs along Lake is NOT stated and is not inferred here. The reconstruction's West Division and Lake-street blocks currently deal their house sizes from archetypes; this is a real one, from the paper, at a corner the plat can find. P. Pruyne is the same timber merchant who sizes the town's structural sticks a fortnight earlier (chicago_democrat_1834_05_07 c012), which is worth noticing: the man selling the frame is also selling the finished house.

claims.notes: A TAVERN CHANGES HANDS AND THE PREMISES ARE 'THAT WELL KNOWN STAND'. The succession chain is explicit — lately occupied by W. Wattles — and the copy dates from October 1833, so this is a standing advertisement seven months old still running in May 1834. That matters twice: it fixes a house of entertainment continuously in the same premises from autumn 1833 through May 1834, and it warns that the advertising columns of this month are not all news. Named the Traveller's Home by its new keeper. No street is printed — 'that well known Stand' is precisely an author relying on the reader already knowing where it is, which is honest evidence of a small town and no evidence of a location, so the placement is none.

claims.notes: THE BAPTIST MEETING HOUSE IS AN ADDRESS ON SOUTH WATER STREET, and this is the first Chicago church used as a placement anchor anywhere in this corpus. A. Filer & Co have COMMENCED — the business is new in May 1834 — three doors from it, making cabinet ware and chairs. Two consequences. First, a meeting house stands on or immediately off South Water street by May 1834 and is prominent enough that a tradesman expects readers to count doors from it; the reconstruction's South Water frontage has no church on it today. Second, the direction word after 'three doors n' is cut at the column edge — it may be north or it may not — and it is NOT supplied, so the shop is three doors from the meeting house on an unstated side. The same firm, as Clark, Filer & Co, advertises chairs from 'the cabinet shop' a week later (chicago_democrat_1834_05_28 c007), so the partnership's name moves inside the month while the premises do not.

claims.notes: WATERPROOF BOOTS, MADE IN CHICAGO, ADVERTISED CONTINUOUSLY FROM DECEMBER 1833. Montgomery is a bespoke bootmaker keeping ready-made work on hand as well — the frontier compromise — and the standing copy date makes him one of the fixed trades of the town rather than a spring arrival. 'Water proof' is not decoration in a town built on a wet prairie: it is what the ground in this reconstruction actually did to footwear, said by a tradesman selling against it. No address is printed and none is guessed.

claims.notes: ONE IMPRESSION OF THE STANDING LAKE STREET LAND-AGENCY CARD. The Democrat sets this advertisement, word for word the same, in every issue from 1834-05-14 to 1834-10-01 — twenty consecutive weeks, eighteen of which set the line ‘purchased and Sold, or by commi[s]sion’ recognisably (T-1051). The card is identified by its copy and not by its display line: the same trade (‘House and Land Agent’), the same offer of building lots in the town and the School Section, the same houses to let, and the same office on Lake street opposite Dr. Temple's. This is the SECOND impression and the first that sets a display line at all: line 2758 reads 'PG. BDRATCULATD,' in a column the transcription itself flags as a Tesseract fallback (line 2757). Nothing is read off it — it is a third mangled setting beside c008's 'Wo. @ WRAWCUA' and 1834-06-04's '@s DRANCRAID,' — and no forename is supplied from it. THE PROPRIETOR'S NAME IS NOT READ HERE and none is supplied into the quote: the record's ‘W. G. Blanchard’ stands on T-0408's reading of the two impressions whose columns are NOT Tesseract fallbacks (1834-07-16 line 5527, 1834-09-17 line 3292) and on identity.json's declared firm merge, not on this impression. The lot count is illegible here ('BD Building Lots'), so it is left unread rather than carried over from the neighbouring weeks.
